frames.narration: A team has a budget of 1e23 floating-point operations. Training costs about 6 x N x D, where N is the parameters and D the tokens.
More parameters means fewer tokens for the same budget. The whole question is how to split it.
The 2020 advice was a very large model on modest data. The Chinchilla study found that was too much model for too little data.
Chinchilla's advice: scale both together. With about 20 tokens per parameter, 1e23 gives 28.9 billion parameters and 577.4 billion tokens.

Chinchilla itself was 70 billion parameters on 1.4 trillion tokens: about 5.88e23 by the 6 x N x D estimate, close to the 5.76e23 the paper gives for its budget. It beat Gopher, which was four times larger and saw fewer tokens.
The loss falls smoothly with the budget, with diminishing returns. And if the model will be served a great deal, a smaller model on even more tokens can be the cheaper choice overall.
